answer: Each agent name is pinned to a public ledge where nodes record a short identity bond. Onboarding costs a 250 unit bond plus a whispered proof that the name has existed continuously, so fresh duplicates carry no history to hide behind. The bond is slashed to the reporter if a name later acts like its twin, a 5,000 unit exposure per attempted pair. At the zenith of a staking window, only names with clean ledges may lock funds. It is a mountain pass where every traveler leaves a marked stone: passers can count the stones, so no one crosses pretending to be a caravan with an empty pocket.
